searchText: You aren't alone in wishing there were more types, particularly hardware native types like 64-bit. Well, yeah 🙂 and if there are none, we should scale the types back There are some EIPs out there that want to constrain some types to 64-bit or 52-bit like gas limit, nonce, etc. (things that will never possibly exceed 52-bits). why 52-bit tho? The largest safe integer that can be exactly stored in a 64-bit floating point. Meaning, you can count from 0 to 2^52 with a double and not miss any numbers. After that you start having holes. This matters because some languages (JS) only have doubles. (technically they now also have unbounded size bigints, but the characteristics of them are very different) And you can only send "numbers" over JSON and JS interprets all JSON numbers as doubles. So... thu more places you can fit things into 52 bits the easier it is for JS integration. JSON strikes again all the more reason to drop jsonrpc lol GRPC wouldn't solve this particular issue. JS still doesn't have integers except for the new `bigint` which is an unbounded size integer and thus different to work with and significantly slower than a 52-bit integer. The `2^52` is mostly a smile towards JavaScript, but you can safely use `i64` for implementation. But it may have some other limiting properties. E.g. for the current `2^63` gas limit the max call depth is ~1500 (because of the 63/64 rule and the call cost). But maybe with `5^52` the max call depth is < 1024 therefore we don't need strictly enforce the 1024 hard limit. The 256-bit `ADDMOD` and `MULMOD` is pretty handy for EC crypto stuff. <@!329594653097721856> if your concern is implementing `u256` then I have C++ library which can be later ported to Rust. I mostly tune it for LLVM or fix LLVM from the other side, so it should play nice in Rust too. we do have U256 and U512 by Parity, but I figured we could move to use native instead
